nodes.name: Call Gemini generateContent
nodes.notes: Model id updated 2026-09-08 to 'gemini-3.6-flash' after live verification against 004-triage: 'gemini-2.0-flash' returned a deprecation error ('This model models/gemini-2.0-flash is no longer available... use models/gemini-3.6-flash') during a real test run, confirmed by triage_error on the affected emails row. Structured output via generationConfig.responseMimeType='application/json' + responseSchema=the caller's response_schema (Gemini's native JSON-mode/schema-constrained generation, not prose parsed after the fact) was confirmed working against the new model id in the same live test. Auth is an HTTP Header Auth credential ('Gemini API', placeholder id REPLACE_WITH_GEMINI_API_CREDENTIAL_ID) whose stored header is 'x-goog-api-key: <API key>' -- set this up in n8n's credential UI on import, matching how gmail-ingestion.json/email-normaliser.json reference not-yet-created credentials by placeholder id + real name. retryOnFail=true/maxTries=3/waitBetweenTries=3000 added after a live transient 'model is currently experiencing high demand' 503 broke a real triage run -- this requires options.response.response.neverError=false (changed from true) so a non-2xx status makes the node genuinely fail and enters n8n's native retry loop, instead of being swallowed as normal response data. onError=continueRegularOutput still applies only AFTER all retries are exhausted: at that point n8n emits a plain { error: <message> } item (not the {statusCode, body} shape), which 'Parse Gemini response' already handles first via its response.error check -- that check was written for exactly this final-failure shape, so no downstream change was needed. options.timeout=30000 added 2026-09-11 during 006-draft-generation live deployment: the caller-side Execute Workflow node has no per-node timeout field in this n8n version's Settings tab (confirmed live, not just suspected), so FR9's 30s hang protection is enforced here instead -- this single HTTP node is the only place in the whole gateway that actually makes a network call, so a timeout here protects every caller (Triage Pipeline, Action Extraction, Draft Generation) at once rather than needing to be set per-caller.

nodes.name: Quota exceeded?
nodes.notes: Routes to OpenRouter ONLY on a genuine Gemini 429/quota exhaustion (statusCode 429, set by 'Parse Gemini response') -- any other failure (network error, malformed response, a real 503) falls through to the false branch unchanged, since those aren't quota problems a fallback provider would fix differently, and silently swallowing a real bug behind a fallback would hide it instead of surfacing it.

nodes.name: Call OpenRouter chat completion

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { "model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json.system_prompt }, { "role": "user", "content": $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json.user_content } ], "response_format": { "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "name": "response_schema", "schema": $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json.response_schema } } } }}

nodes.notes: Fallback provider (L27): fires only when Gemini's daily free-tier quota (20 req/day, gemini-3.6-flash) is exhausted for the day. Model 'openai/gpt-4o-mini' chosen for low cost and json_schema structured-output support, matching Gemini's own schema-constrained generation. Reuses the exact same { system_prompt, user_content, response_schema } contract callers already pass in -- read via the explicit $('Execute Workflow Trigger') reference since this node sits several steps downstream. Not strict-mode json_schema (no 'strict': true) because callers' schemas (e.g. Action Extraction's optional 'deadline') don't list every property as required, which OpenAI's strict mode would reject. Auth is an HTTP Header Auth credential ('OpenRouter API', placeholder id REPLACE_WITH_OPENROUTER_CREDENTIAL_ID) whose stored header is 'Authorization: Bearer <API key>' -- set this up in n8n's credential UI on import, same pattern as the 'Gemini API' credential this file's other HTTP node already documents.

nodes.name: Return result
nodes.notes: Single unified terminal node for both the Gemini-success path and the OpenRouter-fallback path. Without this, the workflow had two differently-shaped terminal branches (Quota exceeded?'s false output ending immediately vs the true branch continuing two more nodes) -- n8n's sub-workflow completion detection raced on that asymmetry and intermittently failed to signal the calling workflow that this execution had finished, even though the correct { success, data } result had already been computed. Confirmed live: Triage Pipeline and Commitment Extraction both silently stopped right after 'Call LLM Gateway' on affected runs, losing real triage/extraction results non-deterministically. A single terminal node removes the race entirely.

json.system_prompt: You are an email triage assistant. Read the email and classify it, then produce a one-line summary. Respond only with JSON matching the given schema.
json.user_content:
Subject: Re: Weekly sync - 3 PM tomorrow?
